thread:
aditya: quick follow-up from the canary rfc — we need to standardize fallback semantics across hosted / dedicated / private. current differences are causing odd edge cases during cutovers.
marie: can you be concrete about the mismatches?
aditya: yeah. hosted has automated region fallback + model-variant translation; dedicated has a reserved pool that expects explicit failover rules; private often disables auto-fallback because of network/acl constraints. result: rollout policies drift per deployment type.
sam: ah. so we have three moving parts: policy expression (what to do), enforcement surface (who makes decision), and translation layer (how we map one model to another in constrained envs).
yuki: telemetry is also a blocker for private — cross-tenant sampling and trace headers get stripped in some customer racks, so our early-warning signals are weaker.
aditya: exactly. proposal: define a compact policy DSL for canary + fallback that is declarative and can be compiled to platform/runtime adapters. one canonical spec, multiple adapters (hosted, dedicated, private).
marie: i like DSL. needs to cover: rollout windows, fail thresholds, cost-safety (max extra tokens), session affinity rules, and a translation table for variant compatibility.
sam: runtime responsibilities: the runtime should evaluate the policy and emit decisions + telemetry. adapters only handle enforcement details (routing, requeue, mutating headers). keeps logic central.
yuki: question: for private/on-prem, customers will often want a control-plane toggle to opt-out of auto-rollbacks. can we model that as a top-level "operator consent" flag in DSL? e.g. operator_consent: required/optional/implicit
aditya: yes — operator_consent is part of the spec but adapters can enforce stronger semantics when constraints require it. also include a "telemetry_fallback_strategy" so if signals drop below X we either pause rollout or reduce traffic.
marie: we should include a small example for readability.
marie: ```yaml
policy_name: quick-canary
window: 10m
traffic_slices: [1, 5, 20, 50]
abort_if: 
  - latency.p95 > 500ms for 3m
  - error_rate >= 0.02 for 2m
operator_consent: optional
telemetry_fallback_strategy: reduce_to: 1%
compatibility_table:
  - from: model-a
    to: model-a-quantized
    tags: [latency-friendly]
```
aditya: adapters would map `abort_if` predicates to local metrics (hosted uses our metrics stream, private maps to customer-provided metrics endpoint or local host metrics).
sam: enforcement question: who has final say when adapter can't satisfy primitive? e.g., private can't route to variant B because it's not present. should adapter return a structured decision back to runtime?
aditya: yes — adapters return Decision.OK | Decision.PENDING | Decision.FALLBACK with optional reason. runtime acts on Decision.FALLBACK immediately, or PENDING triggers a stabilize window. keep protocol small.
yuki: small protocol is good. we must avoid coupling the runtime to vendor-specific error codes. Decision should be generic strings and a freeform reason for logs.
marie: also record a canonical event for audit: {policy, decision, reason, actor, vector}. at minimum the entry should include policy id and variant mapping used.
aditya: agreed. that helps postmortems. infra-bot: deploybot: canary-policy-v2 applied to staging (rollout 10% -> 20%) :rocket:
sam: :thumbsup: next steps?
aditya: 1) draft DSL PR (small subset) 2) runtime adapter shim RFC (protocol + minimal enum) 3) telemetry contract for private (sampling/forwarding requirements) 4) implement a reference adapter for dedicated.
yuki: i'll prototype minimal telemetry shim for private that exposes host metrics to runtime via a signed agent.
marie: i'll write the DSL PR draft. keeping it tiny helps adoption.
aditya: tagging @sam to own the adapter RFC and decision enum.
sam: on it. i'll draft this week.
aditya: cool. can we reconvene next Tue to review the DSL sample and adapter proto?
marie: ✅
yuki: ✅

aditya: thanks — I'll create the GH issues and link back here.
